name: The Woke Salaryman
why_follow: Hand-drawn comic carousels turn complex money topics into one-screen mental models any reader remembers.
style_notes: Two-tone visuals, conversational tone, every comic ends with a clear takeaway line. Hooks lead with a relatable salaryman dilemma.

name: Dawn Cher (SG Budget Babe)
why_follow: Personal-finance OG who blends budgeting, investing, and family money decisions with founder-level transparency.
style_notes: Long-form blog plus short IG captions that summarise. Hooks often start with a real life-stage milestone (renovation, kid, market dip).

name: Chris Chong (Honey Money SG)
why_follow: Walks through real numbers and CPF/SRS optimisation moves the way an FC would in a review meeting.
style_notes: Talking-head plus screen-share with annotated screenshots. Hooks frame a specific dollar outcome ('how I avoided $X tax').

name: Josh Tan (TheAstuteParent)
why_follow: Licensed FC who breaks down insurance and retirement product mechanics in plain language for parents and families.
style_notes: Calm explainer voice, whiteboard-style breakdowns, hooks that name a specific product or scenario ('Should I keep my AIA Pro Achiever?').

name: Kelvin Tan (Kelvin Learns Investing)
why_follow: Casual Singlish-flavoured explainers that make ETFs, credit cards, and SG-specific investing approachable for first-time investors.
style_notes: Sit-down monologue with screen overlays. Hooks lean into self-deprecation and curiosity ('I tried this for 30 days').

name: Loo Cheng Chuan (1M65)
why_follow: Founder of the 1M65 movement; the clearest evangelist of using CPF mechanics for retirement, with proof-of-concept transparency.
style_notes: Direct, mission-led tone. Hooks frame retirement targets in concrete dollar milestones (1M65, 4M65). Strong family-finance framing.

name: Christopher Tan (Providend)
why_follow: CEO of Singapore's first fee-only advisory firm; models how a senior advisor talks about money, life, and retirement without product-pitch energy.
style_notes: Reflective, principle-led writing. Long-form posts on Business Times Money Wisdom column adapted to LinkedIn. Hooks often pose a big-life question.

name: Kyith Ng (Investment Moats)
why_follow: Decades-deep blogger now at a fee-only advisory firm; rare combo of analytical rigor and lived FIRE experience.
style_notes: Data-heavy posts with charts and personal spending logs. Hooks frame a specific portfolio/spending question and walk through the math.

name: Financial Horse
why_follow: SGX-recognised commentator on SG stocks, REITs, and macro - useful for FCs who get asked 'should I buy X right now' by clients.
style_notes: Plain-English market commentary, weekly thoughts roundup format. Hooks tie a single stock or news event to a 'so what' for retail investors.

name: Heartland Boy
why_follow: Heartlander voice on HDB, property, and household finance - speaks directly to the BTO/young-family money decisions FCs walk clients through.
style_notes: Story-led blog posts, candid about wins and losses. Hooks anchor on a relatable household financial moment.

name: Danielle Teboul (Expat Finances)
why_follow: Niche-but-clear voice for the expat client segment most FCs serve at least a few of - shows how to write for a specific audience.
style_notes: Infographic carousels with a single-question hook and a structured 3-5 point breakdown. Tone is warm and practical.

name: Grace Koh
why_follow: SG financial advisor who has built a personal-finance content brand for Gen Z without leaning on recruit-flavoured content.
style_notes: Lifestyle-meets-finance Reels, casual delivery, hooks framed as 'what nobody told me about X'. Strong CTA hygiene.
verification_note: Listed in 2025/2026 SG fin-influencer roundups; double-check post recency directly on the profile before recommending widely.

name: Chris Chong (Honey Money SG) - IG
why_follow: Bite-sized IG companion to the long-form YouTube; useful for studying how a single CPF/SRS idea gets adapted into a 30-second Reel.
style_notes: Quick spreadsheet zoom-ins, on-screen captions, hooks that quote a dollar figure or 'mistake' upfront.

name: The Woke Salaryman - TikTok
why_follow: Comic-format ideas adapted to short video - great study for FCs who want to translate a static carousel idea into a 30-60s clip.
style_notes: Animated comic frames with voiceover or captions. Hooks open on a stark contrast ('rich friend vs broke friend at 35').

name: MoneySmart SG
why_follow: Brand account but a useful pattern library - meme-led TikToks that turn dry product comparisons into watchable hooks.
style_notes: Trend-aware, meme overlays, hooks lean on 'POV' and 'you vs your friend' framings. Always pairs entertainment with one usable tip.

name: 1M65 (Loo Cheng Chuan) - YouTube
why_follow: Daily-cadence podcast format is rare in SG personal-finance YouTube - shows what consistency looks like at volume.
style_notes: Conversational podcast tone, recurring segments around CPF mechanics. Hooks tie one daily money idea to long-term retirement maths.

name: Kelvin Learns Investing - TikTok
why_follow: Long-form YouTube ideas chopped into 30-60s TikToks - useful pattern study for repurposing one idea across formats.
style_notes: Selfie-style talking head, jump cuts, hooks lean on numbers ('I made $X doing this') without crossing into hype.
